review_comments.body: `asyncio` is referenced in the scene export block (`asyncio.get_event_loop()...`) but not imported anywhere in this script. If `SAVE_SCENE_TO` is enabled this will crash with `NameError`; add an `import asyncio` with the other stdlib imports.

`isaac-sim-gui` now launches `bash /isaac-sim/AirStack/simulation/isaac-sim/docker/tmux_gui_with_shell.sh`, but that script does not exist in the repository. Either add the script to `simulation/isaac-sim/docker/` (and mount it) or revert to a known existing entrypoint (e.g., `/isaac-sim/runapp.sh`).

This docstring still says the script spawns an "Ouster lidar", but the implementation now uses `add_rtx_lidar_subgraph`. Update the bullet to avoid misleading users about which sensor pipeline is being exercised.

`sensor_msgs_py` is imported by the node (`from sensor_msgs_py import point_cloud2`) but the package.xml does not declare a dependency on the `sensor_msgs_py` ROS package. Add it as a `<depend>`/`<exec_depend>` so the runtime Python module is guaranteed to be present.

`read_points(..., skip_nans=True)` filters NaNs but not +/-Inf. As a result, infinite points can pass through and be published, despite callers/docs expecting invalid points to be removed. Consider filtering with `np.isfinite` (or similar) before computing `r2`/publishing.

The current implementation materializes the point cloud multiple times (`list(read_points(...))` → list comprehension → numpy array → list again). For typical LiDAR clouds this can add significant latency and memory pressure. Consider using a numpy-based extraction path (e.g., reading directly from `msg.data` / a `read_points_numpy`-style helper) and publishing from a single array to avoid extra copies.

The new lidar filter defaults to subscribing to `/.../sensors/ouster/point_cloud_raw`, and the example Isaac scripts set `lidar_topic_name="point_cloud_raw"`, but the sim→robot bridge forwards only `/.../sensors/ouster/point_cloud`. In sim→robot mode this prevents the filter from receiving data. Add a bridge entry for `/robot_1/sensors/ouster/point_cloud_raw` (and keep `/point_cloud` if needed) or align the published topic name with what’s bridged.

This launch script switches to `add_rtx_lidar_subgraph` but does not set `lidar_topic_name`, while the example scripts explicitly publish `point_cloud_raw` to feed the new `lidar_point_cloud_filter` defaults. Consider setting `lidar_topic_name="point_cloud_raw"` here too (or otherwise documenting/aligning the expected raw vs filtered topic names).

Same as the first drone: `lidar_topic_name` is omitted here, but other launch scripts publish `point_cloud_raw` to integrate with the new point cloud filter. Setting it explicitly avoids topic-name drift across examples and makes the filtering pipeline work out of the box.

This doc claims the filter removes "NaN or infinite" points, but the current implementation only uses `skip_nans=True` (NaNs) and does not explicitly filter +/-Inf. Either update the implementation to drop non-finite points or adjust the wording to match behavior.

`asyncio` is no longer imported in this file (it was removed from the stdlib import block), but it’s still referenced later in the scene export section (`asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(...)`). This will raise `NameError` when `SAVE_SCENE_TO` is enabled; add back an `import asyncio` (or adjust the export code to avoid it).

`check_lidar_filtered_cloud_sanity()` returns only a 2-tuple when there are fewer robot containers than `env["num_robots"]`, but callers (e.g. `test_sensors.py`) unpack three values `(ok, msg, rates)`. This will raise a `ValueError` at runtime instead of producing a clear test failure. Return a consistent 3-tuple (e.g. include an empty rates dict) on this early-exit path, matching the other branches in this function.

This script uses `asyncio.get_event_loop()` when `SAVE_SCENE_TO` is set, but `asyncio` is never imported. Setting `SAVE_SCENE_TO` will raise `NameError: name 'asyncio' is not defined`. Add the missing import (or avoid asyncio usage) so the optional export path works.

The optional `SAVE_SCENE_TO` export path later in this script uses `asyncio.get_event_loop()`, but `asyncio` is no longer imported in the updated import block. If `SAVE_SCENE_TO` is enabled, the script will raise `NameError: name 'asyncio' is not defined`. Add the `asyncio` import (or refactor that block) to keep scene export working.

The module docstring still claims this example spawns an "Ouster lidar", but the implementation was switched to `add_rtx_lidar_subgraph` (RTX OmniLidar) with `lidar_config="ouster_os1"`. Update the docstring wording to reflect RTX OmniLidar to avoid confusing users following this example.

`lidar_point_cloud_filter_node.py` imports `sensor_msgs_py.point_cloud2`, but this package is not declared as a dependency in `package.xml`. Relying on it transitively can break builds in slimmer environments and makes the dependency graph inaccurate. Add the appropriate dependency entry for `sensor_msgs_py` (or the package that provides `sensor_msgs_py`) so `rosdep`/colcon can resolve it correctly.

The docstring suggests running `-m "liveliness and sensors"` to execute both suites, but pytest’s marker expression semantics mean `and` selects tests that have *both* marks (likely none). To run both classes you want `-m "liveliness or sensors"` (or run without `-m`), and the “two bring-up cycles” note should reference that.

In `test_sensor_streams_stable`, `rates = {**rates_sim, **rates_rsd, **rates_lidar}` overwrites entries because sim-side and robot-side stereo/depth use the same topic names. This drops one side’s samples from `metrics.json`. Consider namespacing the keys (e.g., prefix with `sim.` / `robot.`) or storing separate dicts so both paths are recorded.

`sim_side_topics()` appends `(“/clock”, n)` for every robot domain, but downstream `parallel_sample_hz()` keys results by topic string, so duplicate `/clock` entries will overwrite each other and you won’t actually validate all domains (and parsing may miss earlier temp files). Either sample `/clock` once (e.g., domain 1) or change the sampling utilities to key by `(topic, domain)`.

`check_lidar_filtered_cloud_sanity()` sometimes returns only `(ok, msg)` (when there are fewer robot containers than expected), but callers unpack `(ok, msg, rates)`. This will raise a `ValueError` and mask the real failure. Make this branch return a 3-tuple consistently (e.g., include an empty dict as the third element).

This section states `-m "liveliness and sensors"` runs both suites, but `and` in pytest’s marker expressions selects tests that have both marks (so it will typically run nothing). To run both, use `-m "liveliness or sensors"` (or omit `-m`), and then the “two full stack cycles per tuple” explanation applies.

The `topics:` section comment says “Camera topics” but camera (and LiDAR) topics are no longer configured below, while the header comment still lists them as bridged. Either add the intended topic mappings back or update the header/comments so this config accurately reflects what `domain_bridge` will bridge.

`ISAAC_SIM_PYTHONPATH` is constructed as `<filtered>:/isaac-sim/...`. If the filtered prefix is empty (e.g., `PYTHONPATH` unset or fully filtered), this produces a leading `:` which adds the current working directory to Python’s import path. Consider guarding against an empty prefix so you don’t accidentally include `.` in `PYTHONPATH`.

This uses `-m "liveliness and sensors"` as an example of running both suites, but pytest’s marker expression `and` selects tests that have both marks (so it will usually run zero tests). Use `-m "liveliness or sensors"` (or omit `-m`) when you want both marks’ test classes, and then the “two bring-ups” explanation applies.

For `isaacsim`, the intended batching is “at most two `ros2 topic hz` clients at once”, but `image_pairs` / `depth_pairs` include topics for *all* robots. With `--num-robots 3` this still launches 6 Hz probes concurrently per batch, which may reintroduce the bridge overload/flakiness this code is trying to avoid. Consider chunking these lists (e.g., batches of 2 topics) rather than probing all robots’ image topics in one pass.

`check_robot_stereo_hz()`’s docstring says Isaac probes are batched so “at most two `ros2 topic hz` clients run at once”, but `image_pairs` / `depth_pairs` include topics for all robots. With multiple robots this still spawns 2×N concurrent Hz probes per batch. If Isaac bridge overload is the motivation, consider chunking by robot or limiting batch size to 2 topics per pass.

review_comments.body: check_if_collided() calls point_in_search_bounds() without holding the planner mutex, but search_bounds_xy_ can be mutated concurrently by set_search_bounds()/clear_search_bounds(). This creates a data race (and potential crash) between the exploration action thread and the planner thread. Prefer calling is_inside_search_bounds() here (which locks), or take the mutex before evaluating the polygon test.

random_walk_config.yaml adds parameters sub_robot_tf_topic and srv_random_walk_toggle_topic, but RandomWalkNode::readParameters() never declares/reads them and the node code doesn't reference them. This makes the config misleading; either wire these parameters into the node or remove them from the config.

gcs_visualizer Python code imports coordination_msgs (PeerProfile) and coordination_bringup (peer_profile/frame_utils), but those packages are not declared as dependencies here. This can break build ordering and runtime in isolated installs. Add <depend>coordination_msgs</depend> and <depend>coordination_bringup</depend> (and any other direct imports) to package.xml.

The fallback URDF lookup uses FindPackageShare('autonomy_bringup')/urdf, but autonomy_bringup has no urdf/ directory in this repo. With the current default urdf_file_path='robot.urdf.xacro', this branch would fail if URDF_FILE isn't set to a package-qualified path. Consider pointing this fallback at robot_descriptions (or another package that actually ships the URDFs), or change the default to a package-qualified path so it always resolves.

PeerProfile.msg claims gps_fix.header.stamp carries the NavSatFix timestamp, but gossip_node overwrites gps_fix.header.stamp at publish time for dedup/ordering. This mismatch can confuse downstream consumers that expect sensor time. Either update this comment to reflect the publish-time semantics, or add a separate gossip timestamp field and preserve the original NavSatFix header.stamp.

Collector option flat_collection=True conflicts with the inline comment (“preserve source folder hierarchy”). If you intend to preserve hierarchy, this should likely remain false; if you intend a flat collection, update the comment accordingly so future readers don’t invert the flag by mistake.

This change updates the default developer configuration (NUM_ROBOTS=2, Isaac script selection) and also introduces a stray typo in the section divider comment. Consider keeping .env defaults conservative (NUM_ROBOTS=1, single-drone script) and documenting multi-robot settings in docs/sample env instead, to avoid surprising users running `airstack up` after pulling.

The OmniGraph SET_VALUES entries are using a ((attr, node_path), value) tuple form, but the Isaac Sim/OmniGraph examples in this repo use a single attribute path string like "<Node>.inputs:<attr>". As written, these values are unlikely to be applied, which would leave domain_id/cameraPrim/width/height/topic/etc. unset and prevent the overhead camera publisher graph from functioning. Update SET_VALUES to use full attribute path strings for each node input.

These timers are created with ROSClock(), but the node’s docstring/log message claims the publish tick is wall-clock (unaffected by sim time). When use_sim_time=true (set in robot.launch.xml for sim), ROS time pauses if /clock stops, so gossip publish/drain will also pause. Use a steady/system clock for these timers (or explicitly disable use_sim_time for this node) if the intent is truly wall-clock behavior.

peer_registry_monitor is installed as scripts/peer_registry_monitor.py but there is no console_scripts entry (and no extensionless wrapper like scripts/gossip_node). This makes the documented command `ros2 run coordination_bringup peer_registry_monitor` fail unless users include the .py suffix. Consider adding a console_scripts entry (or adding an executable wrapper without .py) to match the docs/README usage.

This module has several unused imports (e.g. copy, gps_to_enu as _gps_to_enu_abs, heading_to_quat, rotate_vector, transform_marker_array). With ament_flake8 enabled for gcs_visualizer, these will fail lint (F401). Either remove the unused imports or re-export/use them intentionally.

This skill refers to a non-existent GCS node/file (`robot_marker_node.py` / `robot_marker_node`). In this PR the implementation appears to be `foxglove_visualizer_node.py` under gcs_visualizer. Update the skill text and file path references so contributors can follow it without hitting missing-file errors.

This path to gossip_payloads.yaml is incorrect for this repo layout; the file added in this PR is under common/ros_packages/coordination/coordination_bringup/config/gossip_payloads.yaml (not robot/ros_ws/src/coordination/...). The defaults set both --input and --output to the same airstack_default.json path. Since gcs startup runs this script on every container start, overwriting the template in-place can cause panel IDs to be re-minted repeatedly (e.g. suffixes stacking) and the layout to drift over restarts. review_comments.body: These raw WebRTC port-forward instructions omit the pinned UDP media port 49099 that the livestream service publishes. Users following this YAML will forward signaling but not SRTP media, resulting in a connected WebRTC client with a blank stream. Update the UDP example to forward 49099 (and remove the obsolete dynamic ranges if they are no longer used).

The NetworkPolicy requirement does not include UDP 49099, but the new livestream path pins SRTP media to 49099/udp. A pool configured from this table could still block the media stream even though TCP signaling works, so add 49099/udp here and remove any obsolete port ranges that are no longer required.

These validation commands still forward the old UDP ranges and omit the pinned 49099/udp media port used by the `isaac-sim-livestream` service. Following this section will leave the WebRTC media path unforwarded, so update the UDP command to forward 49099.

This description says the OSMO flow needs no local AirStack clone, but the tutorial's prerequisites and setup steps require cloning the repo so the `airstack osmo:*` wrappers and workflow YAML are available. Please remove the “no AirStack clone” claim or reword it to distinguish the laptop clone from the pod's separate clone.

`UseKeychain` is a macOS-specific OpenSSH option; Linux OpenSSH clients generally fail with “Bad configuration option: usekeychain” rather than ignoring it. Because this tutorial targets Linux too, add `IgnoreUnknown UseKeychain` before this option or split the macOS-only setting into a separate note.

The suggested Isaac Sim log container name does not match the service started by the default OSMO livestream profile, which sets `container_name: isaac-sim-livestream`. Users copying this command will get a “No such container” error; update the log hint to use the livestream container name (or print different names based on `ISAAC_SIM_LIVESTREAM`).

The expected Compose milestone uses the project-prefixed service name, but the livestream service declares `container_name: isaac-sim-livestream`, so Docker Compose will report/start that fixed name instead. Please align the milestone with the actual container name so users do not misdiagnose startup.

This issue also appears in the following locations of the same file:
- line 364
- line 561

The version is bumped to `0.18.0-alpha.11`, but `CHANGELOG.md` has no corresponding entry for this release. Add the OSMO changes to the changelog under the same version so the release metadata stays consistent with the version bump.

`ISAAC_SIM_LIVESTREAM_UDP_PORT` is parsed with `int(...)` without validation; a non-numeric value will raise `ValueError` and crash the launch script before Isaac Sim starts. Consider guarding with a try/except, validating the port range (1-65535), and falling back to 49099 with a clear log/warn message.

The workflow hard-codes `VERSION: "droan_gl_test"`, which will override `.env` and likely cause inner `docker compose` pulls to fail unless images are published with that exact tag. For a user-facing recommended workflow, this should be removed or set to a known-published version/tag (or left unset so `.env`/defaults apply).

Top-of-file port-forward instructions still reference the old WebRTC port ranges (47995–48012, 49000–49007) and do not include the pinned UDP media port 49099. Since the stack now pins media to 49099 and signaling to 49100, these example commands should be updated to avoid users getting a black stream.

`osmo:ide` relies on `nc -z` to detect when the local port-forward is listening, but `nc` is not guaranteed to be installed on all target hosts (especially Windows setups). Consider checking for `nc` and falling back to a bash `/dev/tcp/host/port` probe (or another portable approach) so `osmo:ide` works with the stated minimal prerequisites.
`json.load(open(pkg_path))` leaves the file handle unclosed. Prefer `with open(pkg_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:` to avoid descriptor leaks and make the read encoding explicit.

After starting Xvfb and waiting up to 10s for `/tmp/.X11-unix/X99`, the script proceeds even if the socket never appears (e.g., Xvfb failed to start). Consider checking for the socket after the loop and emitting an error / exiting (or at least logging) so headless GUI failures are easier to diagnose.

review_comments.body: BodyBinding.from_dict rejects an explicitly empty target_prim (""), but the rest of the config model/docs treat an empty target as valid (e.g., UI can add a body before it’s pointed). This also breaks NatNetInterfaceConfig.to_dict() -> from_dict() round-trips when target_prim is "".

The doc says frames are encoded in “NatNet 4.1 wire format”, but the emulator config and tests advertise/use NatNet 4.4 (e.g., default natnet_version is 4.4.0.0). This is likely to confuse users when validating against libNatNet 4.4.

The documented default publish rate is 120 Hz, but the code defaults to 100 Hz (NatNetInterfaceConfig.DEFAULT_PUBLISH_RATE=100.0 and schema default natnet:publishRate=100). The docs should match the actual defaults to avoid mismatched expectations.

The troubleshooting section still references SITL_PARAM_PROFILE=px4-vision, but earlier in this doc (and in the new sim override) the EV configuration is described via PX4_PARAM_SET=external-vision. Mixing both in one doc is contradictory and will send users down the wrong configuration path.

The module docstring claims this path is “Pure Python + ctypes”, but the implementation imports NumPy and SciPy (Rotation). Either make those imports optional/lazy, or update the docstring to reflect the actual dependencies and fix the missing space in the MODELDEF note.
Trailing whitespace in the module docstring (line ends with an extra space). This can cause lint noise and makes diffs harder to read.
